title: The voltage of a chemical cell
goal: See how the voltage of a voltaic cell depends on the standard electrode potentials of its two half-cells.
note: A voltaic cell joins two half-cells. The half-cell with the more positive electrode potential is the positive terminal, and the cell voltage is its potential minus the potential of the negative terminal.

controls.label: Electrode potential of the positive half-cell

graphs.title: The cell voltage rises in a straight line as the positive half-cell's potential rises.
graphs.label: Cell voltage

sentences: The negative half-cell is a zinc electrode, the metal with the more negative electrode potential.
The cell voltage is the electrode potential of the positive terminal minus that of the negative terminal.

predict.prompt: A zinc half-cell is joined to a half-cell with a more positive electrode potential. What happens to the cell voltage as the difference between the two potentials grows?
predict.reveal: Raise the electrode potential of the positive half-cell and watch the cell voltage.

concept_check.question: How is the standard cell voltage of a voltaic cell found?
options: Add the two standard electrode potentials
Subtract the potential of the anode from the potential of the cathode
Subtract the potential of the cathode from the potential of the anode
concept_check.explanation: The cell voltage is the electrode potential of the cathode, the positive terminal, minus the electrode potential of the anode, the negative terminal.

hints: Each half-cell has its own standard electrode potential.
Which half-cell has the more positive potential? That is the positive terminal.
Subtract the potential of the negative terminal from the potential of the positive terminal.
